requests.submitted_prose: The Supreme Court's identified controversy over tenancy continuance, terms and duration is a subject for civil adjudication rather than determination as a Section 50 trust-affairs inquiry. This procedural subject-matter conclusion does not establish the existence, validity, duration or continued operation of the plaintiffs' asserted tenancy.

checked_scope.statement: Where meaningful reading of the plaint identifies a substantive tenancy-continuance or tenancy-term controversy, those questions are for civil-court adjudication rather than determination as a Section 50 trust-affairs inquiry.
rule_scope_limits: Only subject-matter suitability for civil tenancy adjudication is addressed; the tenancy's existence, duration, continuing validity, and plaintiffs' ultimate rights are not resolved.
The judgment says a tenant is not, by that status, a person having an interest in the trust for Section 51.
This does not independently decide every possible Section 80 objection or whether a different civil court is the proper forum.

requests.published_conditional_statement: Where meaningful reading of the plaint identifies a substantive tenancy-continuance or tenancy-term controversy, those questions are for civil-court adjudication rather than determination as a Section 50 trust-affairs inquiry.

requests.submitted_prose: The distinct prayer for inquiry into alleged trust misconduct follows the Section 50 trust-affairs route and the applicable Section 51 consent regime. This classification neither proves trust misconduct nor establishes whether the required consent was sought or obtained.

checked_scope.statement: A genuine trust-affairs inquiry prayer is treated under Section 50 and the applicable Section 51 consent regime rather than being converted into an ordinary tenancy question.
rule_scope_limits: Section 51's prior-consent requirement is described for suits of the nature specified in Section 50; it is not imposed on every dispute with a trust.
The Commissioner who is asked to inquire is not the trust or its trustees, and the trust inquiry is not the same transaction as the tenancy.
The judgment does not supply proof of either a consent application or consent's absence, and it does not establish trust misconduct.

requests.published_conditional_statement: A genuine trust-affairs inquiry prayer is treated under Section 50 and the applicable Section 51 consent regime rather than being converted into an ordinary tenancy question.

requests.submitted_prose: The presence of a special-Act trust-inquiry prayer alongside a civil-adjudicable tenancy controversy does not alone justify rejection of the whole plaint under Order VII Rule 11(a) or (d). This does not foreclose another properly established whole-plaint ground for rejection or prove that any requested remedy must be granted.

checked_scope.statement: When a whole-plaint review identifies a civil-adjudicable tenancy subject alongside a separate special-Act trust-inquiry prayer, the mere combination of those prayers does not itself justify rejecting the entire plaint; lawful restriction to tenancy issues and applications to relinquish other prayers are distinct procedural matters.
rule_scope_limits: This is a non-entailment rule: mixing prayers is not itself a sufficient Rule 11(a)/(d) ground. It does not immunize an otherwise defective plaint.
Only rejection of the whole plaint is tested here; partial rejection under Rule 11 is not authorized.
A relinquishment request must be addressed to the trial court under the applicable rules; Order II Rules 1 and 2 address claims omitted or intentionally relinquished.

The target court ultimately restricted adjudication to tenancy, tenancy terms and period, despite noting other civil-court-considerable prayers; this registry does not convert those prayers into granted relief.

requests.published_conditional_statement: When a whole-plaint review identifies a civil-adjudicable tenancy subject alongside a separate special-Act trust-inquiry prayer, the mere combination of those prayers does not itself justify rejecting the entire plaint; lawful restriction to tenancy issues and applications to relinquish other prayers are distinct procedural matters.

requests.submitted_prose: The plaintiffs' allegation of forcible eviction and the respondent trust's contrary assertion of lawful possession-taking are both recorded. Their opposition establishes neither actual unlawful dispossession nor voluntary surrender by these plaintiffs.

checked_scope.statement: The litigants advance contrary versions of the identified dispossession, without that record itself proving a forcible ouster, voluntary surrender by the same plaintiffs, or lawful taking of possession.
checked_scope.time_scope: Disputed possession-taking concerning the suit properties; precise event dates are not supplied.
rule_scope_limits: TRUE applies to the recording of both assertions, not to the truth of either description of dispossession.
The judgment reports surrender by 22 of 44 tenants as a trust-counsel point; it does not identify the surrenders as the plaintiffs' acts.
The court notes controversy surrounding how long the trial court injunction operated; no chronology sufficient to resolve the merits is supplied.

requests.published_conditional_statement: The litigants advance contrary versions of the identified dispossession, without that record itself proving a forcible ouster, voluntary surrender by the same plaintiffs, or lawful taking of possession.

requests.submitted_prose: The procedural availability of civil adjudication concerning tenancy does not establish forcible dispossession, a right to restoration under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, or entitlement to an injunction. The disputed possession event and the separate discretionary injunction questions remain matters for relevant evidence and appropriate merits assessment. This is an analytically supported distinction, not a completed mechanical evaluation or a substantive merits ruling.

checked_scope.statement: Procedural survival of the tenancy issue cannot itself establish forcible dispossession, a right to Section 6 recovery, or entitlement to injunction; relevant evidence and discretionary injunction standards must be assessed separately in the appropriate trial proceedings.
checked_scope.time_scope: Supreme Court plaint-rejection review; the relevant periods of settled possession, alleged dispossession and the trial injunction remain unresolved.
rule_scope_limits: Section 6 restoration and discretionary injunction are different questions: possible recovery despite lack of title does not itself justify injunction against a true owner.

The judgment recounts a rule against injunction for a person in unlawful possession against the true owner, but does not find that these specific plaintiffs were unlawful possessors or that an injunction is due or barred on their merits.
The Supreme Court expressly leaves forcible-dispossession issues to the trial court if raised and relevant, and offers no view on the merits.
Claims about arrears, compliance with prior High Court orders, and surrender by other tenants are trust-side submissions or matters left for trial; their significance cannot be presumed.
The separate objection that only the District Court had jurisdiction was not specifically urged below and received no Supreme Court ruling.

policy: Submitted natural-language prose is displayed only as an unverified claim; the conditional conclusion is rendered from the reviewed rule and explicit binding.
interpretation: This display prevents status labels from endorsing arbitrary prose. It does not detect semantic errors in prose or approved translations.
